notes:
START -- agrees with chronicle, but not with the header. The header's Start is 'Any San d'Oria Gate Guard', a CLASS of NPC and not a name; chronicle's row says 'ambrotien'. I write Ambrotien, so the ladder's start folds to exactly chronicle's key and giver_of moves nothing. data/npc_overrides.lua already maps that same generic string to Ambrotien, Endracion and Grilau with zone=false, so chronicle's own resolution keeps by_npc rows on all three guards; naming the class here instead would have resolved to the same first key with nothing gained. start.zone is deliberately null: the mission is offered in three districts and pinning one district would be a claim the page does not make and would fight chronicle's zone=false. Flagged generic_npc_name.

LADDER. Bullets 3, 4 and 5 are one journey -- enter the Quicksand Caves on Map 2 from Eastern Altepa Desert (H-10), drop the hole at (E-11) into the isolated section, walk to the Fountain of Kings at (G-14) -- so they are one travel rung with the route in the note; the Unity Warp alternative is route advice, not a rung. Bullet 6 is TWO rungs, the check that spawns the pair and the fight itself, and bullet 7 is the second check on the same object: that is the page's own sequence (check, kill, check again) and not a split I invented. The two Princes' quarters doors under bullet 2 are the page's own '(Optional)' and give short cutscenes only, so they are not rungs. Bullet 9's one Earth minute is timing, not a rung; the rung is exiting the Chateau into Northern San d'Oria.

EVIDENCE. Drops of Amnio (KI 288) is the only thing in this mission the client will report. It is granted AT the second Fountain of Kings check, and the header's Reward is 'Rank Points' only, so it is not a reward masquerading as evidence. It then rides as `items` on the turn-in to Halver, which is a requirement and not a second evidence claim. Nothing else here is observable: no packet reports the cutscene, the hole, or the kills.

LAG. Between Halver and the Fountain of Kings nothing can be read, so the high-water mark sits on Halver for the whole Quicksand Caves leg. That is the safe direction the runtime documents and there is nothing better to read.

notes:
START. Same generic header as the rest of the San d'Oria line -- 'Any San d'Oria Gate Guard' -- against chronicle's 'ambrotien'. I write Ambrotien, which folds to chronicle's own key, so nothing moves; start.zone stays null because the mission is offered at guards in three districts and chronicle matches them with zone=false. Flagged generic_npc_name.

THE DOOR NAME. The page writes 'the Great Hall door'. That string is a description, not an entity: the entity is 'Door: Great Hall', which San d'Oria Mission 3-3 in this same corpus writes out ('Click the Door: Great Hall behind Halver'). I use the entity form so the marker can resolve; 'great hall door' folds to a key nothing in game answers to. Same door at steps 1 and 10.

EVIDENCE, and what I refused. Crystal dowser (KI 284) is handed over by Rahal at step 2 and is not in Reward (Rank 9 and 80,000 gil), so it is real evidence at its own step. Prelate Key (item 1137) is likewise obtained at the farm step and reads true the moment you hold one -- including one farmed before the mission, which is correct, since that step exists only to get you one. It is then carried as `items` on the door rung. Flagged consumed_key_item because the page never says whether the key survives opening the door; if it is eaten there the evidence stops reading true and the mark can regress across a logout, which the per-session latch hides but does not cure.

The three Piece of a broken key ??? are ONE rung, not three. They are the same entity name in the same hallway of the same zone, the page says any order, and the count cannot be observed: the three pieces share one key item name and resolve to ids 285-287 with 'hold ANY id' semantics, so evidence there would fire on the FIRST piece and walk the mark to the doll door while two pieces were still missing. No evidence on that rung, flagged count_unobservable and unordered_group, with the three grids in its note.

WHAT IS NOT NAMED. Two doors carry rungs and neither is named: 'the door at (I-10)' the Temple Guardian opens, and 'the door at (J-10)' the Prelate Key opens, plus 'the second door (H-10)' that spawns the dolls. I record them as unnamed targets rather than inventing names; they keep their rungs and lose only their markers. Flagged unnamed_target.

The key can also be farmed from Tonberry Choppers in Yhoator Jungle or Tonberry Slashers in the Den of Rancor. Those are other ZONES and a step has one zone, so only the page's primary source is modelled and the alternatives live in the note -- flagged or_branch_unmodelled. Bullet 10 is the reward, not a step.

  step 6: the right one answers 'Obtained key item: Piece of a broken key.' One rung rather than three: same entity name, same zone, and the three pieces share one key item name (ids 285-287, any of which reads true), so a per-piece count is not observable.

notes:
START. 'Any San d'Oria Gate Guard' in the header against chronicle's 'ambrotien'; I write Ambrotien, which folds to chronicle's key, so the marker does not move. start.zone null for the same reason as the rest of the line -- three districts, chronicle matches with zone=false. Flagged generic_npc_name.

THE WALKTHROUGH IS THREE BULLETS AND THE MISSION IS NOT. Bullet 3 says only 'travel to 3 ??? and obtain 3 Key Items'; the actual instructions are in the three sibling sections 'After the walkthrough: Valley of Sorrows', ': Xarcabard' and ': Batallia Downs'. Those hold the rest of the mission, so steps 2 through 7 come from them and their numbering restarts at [1] -- each step's note names the section it came from. Flagged steps_from_after_section.

Bullet 1 is the page's own '(Optional)': Princes' Quarters door cutscenes and small talk with Curilla and Rahal. Flavour, not rungs, and not recorded -- marking them would put the mission's marker on people who advance nothing.

THE THREE FIGURES ARE AN UNORDERED SET, and I have modelled them as one, but a reader should know what that costs. Each ??? grants its own distinct key item -- Figure of Titan (483), Garuda (482), Leviathan (481) -- none of them in Reward (Rank Points), so each is honest evidence at its own step. The runtime's position rule is a HIGH-WATER MARK (1 + the highest step whose evidence reads true), so doing them out of the page's order can put the mark ahead of the player: getting Leviathan first reads as step 7. In practice that costs almost nothing here, because step 7's target is the SAME entity as step 1's -- Door: Great Hall -- so the marker sits on the Chateau door either way, and the ??? themselves can never carry a marker. In the page's own order the ladder tracks correctly. I would rather record the three key items honestly and say this than collapse them into one AND-list that would never let the mark reach the Suparna fight.

The group 'figures' is on the three ??? that OPEN each errand. The Batallia Downs one continues into an ordered fight and a second check, so steps 5 and 6 are deliberately not group members.

DOOR NAME. The page writes 'the Great Hall door'; the entity is 'Door: Great Hall', as San d'Oria Mission 3-3 writes it. Used at steps 1 and 7.

The Eldieme Necropolis route to the Batallia island is travel advice and rides in a note rather than becoming a rung -- a marker in a corridor zone would point at somewhere you only pass through. Ahtu is the page's own 'Optional' and is not recorded.

steps.note: the page says 'the Great Hall door'; the entity name is Door: Great Hall, as San d'Oria Mission 3-3 writes it. Bullet 1 above it is the page's own '(Optional)' flavour and is not a rung.

from 'After the walkthrough: Valley of Sorrows', bullet [1] -- that section's numbering restarts. Sneak and Invisible across unless you have a mount; the Survival Guide uses the same entrance, or the Unity Warp (Level 135), or in from Cape Teriggan at (J-8).

from 'After the walkthrough: Xarcabard', bullets [1]-[3], whose numbering restarts. Upper level, in a clump of three trees with their leaves west of the ramp, still in (H-7); the Survival Guide lands at (H-9), almost due south of the ramp.

from 'After the walkthrough: Batallia Downs', bullets [1]-[4], numbering restarts. The island is only reachable through the Eldieme Necropolis: in at (I-10), through the southern room to the centre hole at (G-9) -- Sneak before dropping -- east along map 2 to map 3, out at (J-9). Several ??? on the island; the one that works is by the Stone Monument at the rear. This is the group member that continues into an ordered fight, so steps 5 and 6 are not in the group.
Suparna is WAR (Mighty Strikes), the Fledgling WHM (Benediction); both use Horde Lullaby and Massacre Elegy. Ahtu on the way in is the page's own optional detour.
the same ??? again, once the corpses despawn; a cutscene comes with the key item
from the Batallia Downs after-section, bullet [6]; this check completes the mission. All three figures must be held.

notes:
START. 'Any San d'Oria Gate Guard' against chronicle's 'ambrotien'; I write Ambrotien, folding to chronicle's own key, so nothing moves. start.zone null -- three districts, chronicle matches with zone=false. Flagged generic_npc_name.

ZERO EVIDENCE, ON PURPOSE. This mission hands over nothing the client will report: its rewards are the title, Rank 10, 100,000 gil, the San d'Orian Flag and the ability to buy the Atma of the Heir, and a reward is not evidence. Six of its eleven bullets are zone lines and cutscenes, which no packet reports. So the mark stays at 1 for the whole mission and, because steps 1 and 2 are zone entries with nothing to mark, the marker falls back to the giver. That is the correct outcome for a mission with nothing observable in it, not a gap in the reading -- the ladder is still worth having for //qm why, which can then say where the mission actually goes.

THE BATTLEFIELD IS ONE RUNG. Bullets 5 and 6 are the two waves of a single Qu'Bia Arena BCNM entered once; nothing separates them that the addon could ever see, so they are one fight step carrying every monster the page names. Prince Trion fights on your side in part two and is NOT recorded as a mob -- he is an ally, and marking him would put a kill glyph on a friend. Bullet 4, getting to the arena, is its own travel rung because it names a route (Fei'Yin Home Point #1 or Domenic, then the Burning Circle room).

NAMES. Heavy Stone Door is the page's own entity name and the same one San d'Oria Mission 6-2 uses in King Ranperre's Tomb, so it is used verbatim. 'the Great Hall door' is the description; 'Door: Great Hall' is the entity, per San d'Oria Mission 3-3. The optional Papal Chamber door under bullet 10, and Arnau under bullet 1, are flavour and are not rungs.
